headline: The research paper repository arXiv has capped each author at two submissions a month because AI tools are driving a flood of low-value papers.
score_reason: Pool score 6 lowered by one: the rule took effect on 1 Oct 2026, before today's window; the facts themselves are solid.
importance_line: Researchers who post to arXiv, the free site where most AI and physics papers first appear, now face monthly limits, and the volunteer moderators who screen papers get relief, though arXiv calls the rule a temporary stopgap.
summary: Research Information reports, quoting arXiv, that the open-access preprint site received a record 40,363 submissions in September 2026, almost double the 20,569 of September 2024. Under a rule that began on 1 October 2026, each author may submit two papers a month and hold at most three active submissions, which arXiv describes as a stopgap while it decides how to handle advanced AI tools.
